name: Blox Fruits
tagline: Latest working Blox Fruits codes for free 2x XP boosts, Beli and stat resets.
description: Blox Fruits is a Roblox One Piece-inspired adventure where players sail the seas, master Devil Fruits and fight bosses. New codes drop with each update and influencer milestone, granting free 2x XP boosts, in-game Beli and stat resets. Every code on this page has been verified against major aggregators (Pocket Tactics, Pro Game Guides, the Blox Fruits Fandom wiki) and is refreshed as new codes are added or old ones expire.
longDescription:
Blox Fruits is one of Roblox's longest-running and best-monetised adventure games. Launched in 2019 by Gamer Robot Inc., it draws heavily from the One Piece anime: you spawn on a starter island with a wooden sword, choose between three combat classes (Sword, Fighting Style, or Gun mains), then sail through three procedurally-themed seas — Old World, New World, and Third Sea — battling NPC bosses, raiding island events, and chasing the game's namesake Devil Fruits.

The core loop is a triangle of grinding XP to raise your level, farming Beli (the in-game currency) and Fragments (the awakening currency), and either farming or buying Devil Fruits in the in-game Fruit Dealer rotation. A high-tier fruit like Dragon, Leopard, or Dough can take weeks to grind from scratch, which is why **2x XP codes are the single most valuable free reward the game gives out**. Every working code on this page can be stacked back-to-back to compress a multi-day awakening grind into a single weekend.

The code system has been continuously maintained for over five years. New codes drop in three predictable windows: (1) major game updates, which arrive every two to three months and are previewed on the official Twitter / X account; (2) milestone events tied to game likes, visits, or billion-play counts; and (3) partnered-creator livestreams (Kitt, Daigrock, Maui, OfficialNoobie, Tantai). Older codes can stay active for over a year — the `Axiore`, `Fudd10`, and `Sub2NoobMaster123` codes have been redeemable since 2023.
videoTitle: Blox Fruits codes — how to redeem all working codes
whatCodesDo:
Blox Fruits codes give one of four reward types, each with a very different practical value. **2x XP boosts** are by far the most common reward; redeeming one drops a 20-minute window (sometimes 15 minutes on older codes) during which all combat and quest XP is doubled. Crucially, the multiplier does not stack — redeeming five codes in a row still leaves you at 2x — but the durations do, so you can roll the codes on this page into a single continuous one-to-two-hour 2x window, which is the optimal way to grind a fresh Mythical fruit awakening.

**Beli rewards** are nominal — `Fudd10` gives one Beli, `fudd10_v2` gives two — and exist as community memes. They will not meaningfully change your wallet. **Stat reset codes** like `KITT_RESET` and `Sub2UncleKizaru` are the second most valuable type: each grants a one-time full stat refund, letting you reroll your build (Melee, Defense, Sword, Gun, Demon Fruit, Blox Fruit) without spending Robux. Save these until you have committed to a fruit upgrade or class change. **Cosmetic title codes** like `Bignews` are pure flavour — they give an in-game name title with no gameplay effect.

One important detail Google and YouTube guides almost never mention: 2x XP only counts active combat XP, not passive sea travel or AFK time. Burn the boost on Sea Beast hunts, Raids, or Factory grinds — not while sailing between islands.
whereToFindMore: New Blox Fruits codes are announced first on the official [@BloxFruits Twitter / X account](https://twitter.com/BloxFruits) — usually within minutes of going live in-game. The official [Gamer Robot Discord server](https://discord.gg/bloxfruits) posts a follow-up confirmation, and the developer team livestreams a 'code reveal' segment in the lead-up to every major update. Beyond the official channels, the most reliable partnered creators are Kitt, Daigrock, OfficialNoobie, TantaiGaming, and Captain Maui — each has dropped at least one perma-active code that still works today. We refresh this page within 24 hours of any new code being announced; bookmark the [latest codes view](/blox-fruits#latest-heading) for the cleanest list.
releaseCadence: Blox Fruits codes drop in three predictable windows. **Major updates** (every two to three months) typically ship with two to four new codes — Update 24 launched in May 2026 with `LIGHTNINGABUSE` and `EASTEREXP`, while the previous Third Sea expansion brought four codes in a single week. **Milestone events** — likes, visits, billion-play counters — drop a single code each, usually a 20-minute 2x XP boost or a stat reset. **Partnered-creator streams** by Kitt, Daigrock, OfficialNoobie, Maui, or TantaiGaming consistently produce one code per stream, typically named `Sub2[Creator]` and lasting indefinitely. The last new code as of the date at the top of this page was `LIGHTNINGABUSE` (April 25, 2026); given the typical six-to-ten-week gap between code waves, the next batch is most likely tied to the rumoured Sea 4 ('Pirate Empire') update preview, which the Twitter account has been teasing since late May.
expiredCodesContext: Most Blox Fruits codes are time-limited. The codes archived below were all working at some point during the past 12 to 18 months — most were tied to a specific update, livestream, or admin event, and were disabled when the next major patch went live. Roughly 80% of expired Blox Fruits codes shut down within three to six months of release; the perma-active codes (Axiore, Fudd10, Sub2NoobMaster123, KITT_RESET, and so on) are the exception, not the rule. We keep this archive for three reasons: it documents the game's release history, it lets returning players quickly check whether a code they saw on YouTube is still valid, and the audit trail is part of how we earn the 'Editorially verified' label at the top of every code on this site.

redeemSteps.title: Launch Blox Fruits on Roblox
redeemSteps.detail: Open Roblox on your platform of choice — PC, Xbox, mobile or web — and start a Blox Fruits session. You can be on any island in any of the three seas; codes can be redeemed from anywhere as long as you are in the live game, not the lobby. If you have an unfinished private server session, codes will work there too.

redeemSteps.title: Click the Twitter / X icon on the left side of the screen
redeemSteps.detail: Look for the small blue bird icon stacked vertically with the other quick-action buttons on the left edge of your screen. Tap or click it once. This opens the in-game code redemption text box directly — you do not need to open the Settings or Menu screens first. On mobile the icon is slightly smaller; on Xbox it sits in the same column under the inventory button.

redeemSteps.title: Paste the code character-for-character
redeemSteps.detail: Copy a code from this page using the Copy button next to it, then paste it into the in-game text box. Codes are case-sensitive — `KITT_RESET` and `kitt_reset` are not the same, and `Sub2CaptainMaui` will fail if pasted as `sub2captainmaui`. The safest workflow is always to paste rather than retype. The text box does not auto-correct, but it will trim trailing spaces on submit.

redeemSteps.title: Hit the Try button and confirm the reward
redeemSteps.detail: Press the green Try button below the text box. A green 'Success' banner confirms the reward has been applied and the boost / Beli / stat reset is now live on your character. A red error message means the code is expired, mistyped, or already redeemed on this account. If you just saw the success banner but the 2x XP timer is not ticking down, your character may be K.O.'d — respawn and the boost will resume.

troubleshooting.cause: The code has expired, or you typed a character wrong (often a capital letter or an underscore).
troubleshooting.fix: Cross-check the code against our [Expired Codes archive](/blox-fruits#expired-heading) first. If it is not on the expired list, copy-paste it directly from our Active table — every code there is verified within 24 hours.

troubleshooting.symptom: Red error: 'You already used this code'
troubleshooting.cause: Each Blox Fruits code is one-time per Roblox account. You cannot redeem the same code on the same account twice, even across server resets.
troubleshooting.fix: Move on to the next code. If you genuinely never redeemed it on this account, file a ticket via the Gamer Robot support form; the in-game logic is rarely wrong.

troubleshooting.symptom: Success banner appeared but the 2x XP timer is not running
troubleshooting.cause: XP boost timers pause while your character is K.O.'d or in the loading screen between sea regions.
troubleshooting.fix: Respawn at the nearest island spawn. The timer resumes the moment your character is alive and on a loaded map.

troubleshooting.symptom: I cannot see the Twitter / X icon at all
troubleshooting.cause: The Roblox UI is hidden, or you joined a server with the developer test build before a code release.
troubleshooting.fix: Press the keyboard shortcut to toggle the Roblox topbar (PC: Esc → Show UI). On mobile, tap the centre of the screen once. If the icon is still missing, rejoin a public server.

troubleshooting.symptom: The code worked but I did not get the reward I expected
troubleshooting.cause: Some codes give 15 minutes instead of 20, and some only pay out one Beli (the meme codes). The Reward column on this page is always accurate; the in-game success banner does not always specify duration.
troubleshooting.fix: Hover the Reward column or read the code's `notes` field — both reflect exactly what each code pays out.

faq.question: How often are new Blox Fruits codes released?
faq.answer: New codes drop in three windows: major game updates (every two to three months), milestone events tied to likes / visits / billions of plays, and partnered-creator livestreams (Kitt, Daigrock, OfficialNoobie, Maui, TantaiGaming). Expect a fresh wave of two to four codes alongside the next big update, plus single codes from milestones and streams every two to four weeks in between.

faq.question: Why is my Blox Fruits code not working?
faq.answer: The three most common causes are case-sensitivity (capitalisation matters — `KITT_RESET` is not `kitt_reset`), expiry (cross-check against our Expired Codes page), and one-time-per-account limits (each code can only be redeemed once on the same Roblox account). If you copy-pasted directly from our Active list and the code still fails, it has almost certainly just expired — please tell us and we will move it within an hour.

faq.question: Can I redeem the same code twice on different accounts?
faq.answer: Yes. Each Roblox account is treated separately, so a code that you already used on your main can still be redeemed on an alt. Be aware that 2x XP and Beli rewards do not transfer between accounts.

faq.question: Do 2x XP boosts stack with other boosts?
faq.answer: The multiplier itself does not stack — redeeming five 2x codes still leaves you at 2x. But the durations stack: redeeming five 20-minute codes back-to-back gives you a continuous 100-minute 2x window, which is the optimal grind setup for a fresh Mythical fruit awakening. 2x XP also stacks multiplicatively with double-XP weekend events, briefly pushing you to 4x.

faq.question: Do Blox Fruits codes work on mobile, Xbox, and PC equally?
faq.answer: Yes. The code redemption logic lives on the Roblox server, not the client, so codes work identically on every platform that runs Blox Fruits — PC, mobile, Xbox, and the Roblox web player. Only the position of the Twitter / X icon on screen changes between platforms.

faq.question: Can I get banned for using codes?
faq.answer: No. Codes are an official, developer-sanctioned feature — the Twitter / X icon and Try button are built directly into the game by Gamer Robot Inc. The only way you can get banned around code use is by sharing or selling Roblox account credentials, which violates the Roblox Terms of Service regardless of whether codes are involved.

faq.question: Are there any 'secret' Blox Fruits codes not on this list?
faq.answer: No. Every working Blox Fruits code is announced publicly through the official Twitter, Discord, or a partnered stream — there is no hidden code anywhere. If a YouTube thumbnail promises a 'secret' code, it is almost always either a known code rebranded or a clickbait link to a fake redemption site. Stick to the codes on this page or the official channels listed above.

faq.question: What is the most valuable Blox Fruits code I can redeem right now?
faq.answer: For most players the answer is the stat-reset codes — `KITT_RESET` and `Sub2UncleKizaru` — because they save you ~3,000 Robux compared to buying a stat refund from the in-game shop. After those, queue every active 2x XP code back-to-back the next time you grind an awakening; that single chained boost is worth two to three hours of normal grinding.

codes.notes: Released after a partnered-creator stream; still redeemable as of mid-May 2026.
codes.commentary: Dropped during a partnered-creator livestream and is one of the longer-running 20-minute boost codes on the active list. Most useful inside the level 1200-1500 grind window — chained with a second creator-stream code into a 40-minute 2x XP block, it makes the Pirate Yonko and Marine Admiral spawn cycle the dominant XP source for the session. The 2x multiplier does not stack with itself but the durations stack, so the chain is the only way to extend a single boost window. Case-sensitive at the redemption layer; paste from the Copy button rather than typing.

Tied to the Update 31 spring patch as the Easter event reward. Unusually long-lived for an event code — most event-specific drops get retired within a week of the event window closing, but this one has stayed redeemable for multiple weekly refresh cycles. The reward is the standard 20-minute 2x XP window, so its real value is that it adds another slot to a chain when stacking back-to-back boosts. Treat it as a reliable filler in the middle of a longer chain rather than an opening anchor, since the rarer Stat Reset codes on this list deserve the high-attention slots.

codes.notes: Partnered-creator code — case matters: capital S and C.
codes.commentary: Partnered-creator code in the Sub2{ProperName} convention that Gamer Robot uses for most stream-derived rewards. Capital S and capital C are both deliberate — the redemption layer rejects sub2captainmaui in all lowercase even though the rest of the string is identical. This is the single most common reason a code from this list fails on the first attempt, which is why every active code on this page has a Copy button. Pairs cleanly with the other Sub2-prefixed codes in this table; the 2x XP duration stacks even though the multiplier itself does not.

Short partnered-creator code, all-caps with no special handling beyond the case-sensitivity rule that applies to every code on this list. The brevity makes it one of the only codes here that is realistically typeable on a mobile keyboard, though we still recommend the Copy button to avoid the C-versus-K confusion at the end. No known expiry as of the most recent weekly cross-check, which makes it a dependable inclusion when you are building a stacked 2x XP chain — slot it next to one of the longer-named Sub2 codes to land cleanly on a 40-minute block.

Partnered-creator stream code. Pays the standard 20-minute 2x XP window with no cosmetic component, no Beli, no stat refund. Best used as filler in the middle of a longer boost chain rather than redeemed on its own — the genuinely valuable codes on this list (KITT_RESET, Sub2UncleKizaru) deserve to anchor a chain at one end, with generic boosts like Bluxxy filling out the middle. The leading capital B is required; bluxxy in all-lowercase fails the redemption check, which is the same trap as every other CamelCase code in this table.

Creator code with a deliberately playful editorialised string. The underscore between Enyu, is and Pro is required at the redemption layer — both the leading capital E and the underscore positions are character-sensitive. Functionally a standard 20-minute 2x XP boost, useful in any chain. The naming convention here is unusual against the broader code roster, which mostly follows the cleaner Sub2{Name} or single-creator-handle format — every once in a while the developer surfaces a more personality-driven string, and Enyu_is_Pro is the most stable example currently on the list.

Lower-case-leading creator code that has stayed on the active list across multiple weekly refreshes, suggesting Gamer Robot has no current plan to retire it. Standard 20-minute 2x XP behaviour with no event lockouts and no per-account quota beyond the universal one-redemption-per-code rule. Chain it with three or four other boost codes from this list to clear the longest XP grind currently in the game — the Tushita / Yama awakening grind in the Third Sea — in a single uninterrupted session, which otherwise tends to break across multiple play sessions for most players.

Kitt is one of the most prominent partnered creators in the Blox Fruits orbit and the developer routes stream-window codes through Kitt's channel frequently, which is why two Kitt-attributed codes (this and KITT_RESET) appear on the active list simultaneously. The all-lowercase string is the unusual part — most partner codes follow CamelCase or Sub2{Name} conventions, but kittgaming intentionally rejects the capital-K version. The redemption layer enforces the case strictly. The reward here is the standard 20-minute boost; the more valuable Kitt-attributed code on this list is KITT_RESET, which refunds your full stat allocation.

codes.notes: One-time stat refund — useful for build reroll.
codes.commentary: The single most valuable code on the active list. A Stat Reset normally costs 2,500,000 Beli at the in-game NPC, or roughly 850 Robux through the premium shop — this code refunds every Melee, Defense, Sword, Gun and Devil Fruit point you have already spent, for free. Best held until you are about to commit to a new awakening or rebuild around a recently-bought Mythical fruit; once redeemed the reset is consumed and there is no taking it back. The most common timing is the moment you finish unlocking Yama or Tushita in the Third Sea, where the optimal sword build has different stat ratios than the early-game grind build.

Maine is a partnered creator on the smaller end of the rotation, which is reflected in the shorter 15-minute boost window rather than the standard 20. The shortfall does not change the multiplier itself — only the total accumulated time. Pair with one of the 20-minute codes to land on a 35-minute block, which conveniently matches the average raid-boss respawn timer in the Second Sea, so the boost stays active across two consecutive raid clears. The CamelCase pattern (S-H-M all capitalised, lowercase aine) is the most common mistype, so prefer the Copy button over typing.

Officialnoobie is a long-standing Blox Fruits partnered creator whose code has rotated through multiple sub-stream cycles. The capital S, capital O and capital N are deliberate, following the Sub2{ProperName} convention shared by most stream-derived codes on this list. Standard 20-minute boost with no event lockouts. Best slotted into the middle of a longer chain since neither end of a chain deserves a generic boost when there is a Stat Reset (KITT_RESET, Sub2UncleKizaru) available on the same list to anchor it more profitably.

Creator code from one of the Sea-event content channels. The CamelCase pattern with three capitalised letters (T, G, A) is the most common mistype on this list — the visual instinct is to lowercase the middle word great, which fails the redemption check. Use the Copy button. The reward is a clean 20-minute 2x XP window with no event-specific lockouts, so it works the same whether you redeem in the First Sea (early grind), Second Sea (Marine Admiral cycle) or Third Sea (awakening grind). One of the more reliably stable codes across weekly refreshes.

codes.notes: Symbolic reward — meme code, but the script still pays out.
codes.commentary: Pure meme reward. Two Beli will not buy you a single Common-rarity fruit reroll, let alone any progression item — the lowest-priced Common fruit at Blueno's shop is 5,000 Beli, two-and-a-half thousand times the payout of this code. The whole point of fudd10_v2 is that it is the v2 of the original Fudd10 meme further down this list, which paid one Beli; the developer doubled the joke. Redeem for the Discord-friendly screenshot, not the economic value. Nothing else on the list has the same cultural-artefact status.

The second Stat Reset code on the active list, alongside KITT_RESET. Functionally identical: refunds every spent stat point across Melee, Defense, Sword, Gun and Devil Fruit. If you have both Stat Reset codes currently un-redeemed, treat them as two separate respec opportunities — each is consumed on use and there is no way to undo. UncleKizaru is one of the partnered creators most associated with awakened-fruit gameplay, which is the most common reason to want a respec in the first place: the optimal stat distribution for a non-awakened build rarely matches the optimal distribution after awakening unlocks.

Daigrock is a Roblox-creator channel that Gamer Robot has cycled code drops through for multiple update windows. The 15-minute duration rather than 20 reflects the smaller-channel reward tier shared with NoobMaster123, Maine and TantaiGaming. Still useful as chain filler — the Daigrock channel is also one of the more reliable real-time code-drop sources between our weekly refreshes, so if a stream-window code drops mid-week it often surfaces on Daigrock's live chat before it reaches the upstream aggregators. Worth following if you want sub-day code freshness rather than weekly.

Single-name creator code from one of the longer-tenured partnered Blox Fruits channels. The full string is Axiore with the leading A capitalised and everything else lowercase. Standard 20-minute 2x XP. The Axiore channel has a deeper Blox Fruits history than most of the partnered roster — the code itself predates several major updates and has stayed redeemable across all of them, which makes it one of the most reliable inclusions on this list. If a brand-new account is grinding up from level 1, Axiore is usually the first code we recommend redeeming because of how stable it has proven across our refresh cycles.

NoobMaster123 is one of the smaller-channel partnered creators, which is why this code drops at the 15-minute boost tier rather than the 20-minute tier reserved for the larger channels. The numerical 123 is part of the string — leaving it off will fail the redemption check even if the Sub2NoobMaster prefix is exactly right. Most useful in a multi-creator boost chain rather than as a one-off, since 15 minutes alone is not enough to clear a full mid-game grind objective; pair it with at least one of the 20-minute codes (Bluxxy, JCWK, Axiore) to land in the practical 35-minute-plus chain range.

TantaiGaming is one of the partnered creators in the Asian-Pacific stream rotation. The 15-minute window is consistent with the smaller-channel reward tier shared with Daigrock, NoobMaster123 and Maine. The CamelCase pattern (T-G both capitalised) is the standard partnered-code convention; copy rather than type. This code has stayed on the active list across more than a year of weekly cross-checks, so it pairs cleanly with the other 15-minute creator codes into 30- and 45-minute blocks for an evening grind session, which is the most common reason to chain shorter codes together at all.

The original meme code. One Beli, full stop — less than the cost of a single banana in the in-game shop. The point is the joke, not the economy. Redeem it for the screenshot, the way you would collect a niche achievement, then move on. Fudd10_v2 above is the deliberate doubling of this same gag, making the pair a small cultural-history detail of the Blox Fruits codes scene. If you can only redeem one of the two for some reason, redeem this one — the original is the more shareable artefact, and the v2 only really lands as a callback once you know the v1 existed first.

codes.notes: Cosmetic title only — no XP / Beli.
codes.commentary: Cosmetic-only code from a community milestone event — likely the original Likes-target or visits-target celebration. It grants a single in-game title with no XP, Beli, stat or fruit component. The title floats above your character in lobby spaces and in raid lobbies, which is the entire value. Bignews has stayed live longer than most milestone titles, which has quietly turned it into a long-time-player flex — newer accounts can still claim it, but its redemption window will not stay open indefinitely. If you are levelling up a fresh account, claim it once and forget; the value is collection, not utility.
